question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
**Yes, by a wide margin.** In the year to **August 2026**, electricity prices rose **13.2%**, while overall CPI rose **4.0%**. That makes electricity inflation more than three times the headline rate. (Source: ABS monthly CPI, original series, Australia, change from a year earlier.)

**Annual change over the past year:**

| Month | Electricity | All groups CPI |
|---|---|---|
| Aug 2025 | 24.6% | 3.2% |
| Oct 2025 | 37.1% | 3.8% |
| Dec 2025 | 21.5% | 3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | 37.0% | 3.7% |
| Apr 2026 | 22.5% | 4.2% |
| Jun 2026 | 22.4% | 3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | 6.1% | 3.5% |
| **Aug 2026** | **13.2%** | **4.0%** |

**What stands out:**
- **Electricity has outpaced overall inflation every month since July 2025.** Annual rates peaked at about 37% in October 2025 and February 2026. The last time it ran below headline in this data was June 2025, when electricity prices were down 6.3% on a year earlier.
- **The gap has narrowed a lot.** Electricity inflation dropped from 22.4% in June 2026 to 6.1% in July, then rose to 13.2% in August. The July drop is probably a "base effect": prices jumped in July 2025, so comparing against that higher level makes the 2026 increase look smaller.
- **The monthly figures are noisy.** Government energy bill rebates, and when they start or end, move measured electricity prices sharply from month to month. The data doesn't break this out, but rebate timing is likely behind much of the swing between about 6% and 37%. It's more reliable to read the trend over several months than any single month.
- **Electricity is likely adding to headline inflation.** Overall CPI is at 4.0%, above the RBA's 2–3% target band, and electricity rising this much faster suggests it is pushing the headline figure up.

The latest data available is for August 2026; September figures haven't been released yet.
